findings.title: Team admin/owner permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`. Because a team member has a single role (either `ADMIN` or `OWNER`), depending on how `isTeamAdmin` is implemented (whether it strictly checks `role === 'ADMIN'`), using `&&` requires both conditions to be true simultaneously. This should use `||` so that either a team admin or a team owner is authorized to add guests.

findings.title: EventManager is initialized with the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: `addGuestsHandler` allows an attendee or team admin/owner (who is not the booking organizer) to add guests, but lines 158-163 build `EventManager` using `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. When an attendee or another team admin calls `addGuests`, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will try to update the calendar event using the caller's credentials and user record rather than the booking organizer's (`booking.user`), causing calendar updates to fail or target the wrong account.

findings.title: Duplicate emails in `input.guests` and case differences bypass deduplication and blacklist checks
findings.body: In `addGuestsHandler`, `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing `booking.attendees` and `blacklistedGuestEmails` using exact case-sensitive string matching (`guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), while `blacklistedGuestEmails` was lowercased on line 71. Additionally, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts` does not enforce uniqueness on `input.guests` (only client-side validation in `AddGuestsDialog` does). Calling the procedure directly with duplicate emails or uppercase characters in `guests` will insert duplicate attendee rows, bypass `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, and send `guests` (rather than `uniqueGuests`) to `sendAddGuestsEmails` on line 168.

findings.title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores event type email disable settings (`disableStandardEmails`)
findings.body: Unlike `sendScheduledEmails`, `sendRescheduledEmails`, and `sendLocationChangeEmails` right above it, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept `eventTypeMetadata` or check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`. Bookings on event types where standard host or attendee emails are disabled will still send emails when guests are added.
